doc.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: How he writes: Wurlitzer piano and pencil
summary: He writes with an old electric piano and has not moved to computers.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. Appreciate that. Do you write at the piano when you write?

I have no keyboard facility but I have an old Wurlitzer electric piano, it was just perfect for me. I can go over and hit a chord or something and say yes or say no or something. But I haven’t gotten into the computer stage, which everybody else — I have a nephew up in Canada who is such a talent, he writes for CBS, Canadian Broadcasting — CBC they call it. And he uses all the new devices. And he’s encouraging me to try to get into that.
I don’t know. There’s something nice about taking a pencil and putting down what’s up here.
